drivingQuestion: Why does the mishna teach both the money case and the vessels case?
outcomeNote: states necessity; the explanation follows in the next unit

segments.he: וְכֵן שְׁנֵי כֵלִים אֶחָד יָפֶה מָנֶה וְאֶחָד יָפֶה אֶלֶף זוּז כּוּ׳. וּצְרִיכָא.
segments.en: The mishna teaches: «And likewise,» in the case of two people who deposited «two vessels, one worth one hundred dinars and one worth one thousand dinars,» and each of the claimants claims that the expensive vessel is his, the bailee gives the small vessel to one of them, and from the proceeds of the sale of the large vessel he gives the value of the small vessel to the other, and the rest of the money is placed in a safe place until Elijah comes. The Gemara comments: «And» it is «necessary» for the tanna to cite both the case of money and the case of vessels.
